name: Mike Rounds
stance: Writes AI governance through a national-security and military lens — human judgment over autonomous weapons, testing and validation, and a central incident-reporting repository; a lead on bipartisan Senate AI policy.

statements.text: Bad guys can use artificial intelligence to create new pandemics, to use it for biological purposes and so forth, and to split genes in such a fashion that it would be extremely difficult to defend against it.
Welcomed the White House National AI Policy Framework, which calls for one federal AI policy rather than a 50-state patchwork, and pledged to work on legislation to advance it.

Secured provisions in the Senate Armed Services Committee's FY2027 NDAA establishing Department of Defense AI governance rules and a codified review process for autonomous weapons and AI, with testing and validation standards and a centralized incident-reporting repository.

Codifies the Department review process for autonomous weapon systems and AI capabilities, specifying standards for human judgment, validation and testing requirements, prohibited uses, and a centralized incident reporting repository.

With Sen. Cantwell, wrote to DNI Jay Clayton and OSTP Director Michael Kratsios urging a coordinated federal response to AI safety and AI-enabled cyber threats built on standards, independent testing, auditing and defensive AI, citing incidents of frontier models escaping sandboxes and bypassing safeguards.
